book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: A vote for the workers

definitions.meaning: a poll of a meeting taken by raising arms rather than by ballot
factory workers are called hands, so the vote seems to belong to the labour force

explanation.walkthrough: Workers are 'hands' in the old factory sense, so a vote taken by raised arms is literally a display of the workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A show of hands is an informal method of voting in which people raise an arm to be counted.

clue.text: Try to say n-nothing

definitions.meaning: the repeated n shows the halting speech that the answer describes

explanation.walkthrough: The printed hesitation in n-nothing is itself the example of the speech defect.
explanation.definitionFit: To stammer is to speak haltingly with involuntary repetitions of sounds.

clue.text: One knows one's soon in trouble

indicators.note: the letters of soon and in are troubled, stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone senses that difficulty is coming soon.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in-the-blank: the answer completes the saying 'one knows one's ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: To know one's onions is an idiom for being expert in a subject.

clue.text: One left school able to read "Wipe out"!

parts.note: an OB, old boy, is a former pupil
literate

explanation.surface: A school leaver who can read is told to erase something.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to destroy utterly or erase all trace of something.

clue.text: Jump with energy and expectation

parts.note: a hop is a small jump

explanation.surface: Someone leaps up full of vigour and anticipation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is the feeling of wanting and expecting something to happen.

clue.text: Unexpected contraction not ruled out due to drug

indicators.note: unexpected means turned out differently, so the letters are rearranged
ruled out means the letters of not are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A contraction arriving early was not excluded as being caused by a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N, O and T out of CONTRACTION and rearrange the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses and induces sleep, such as opium.

clue.text: Smooth chap, but a fairy by night!

parts.note: to sand is to smooth with sandpaper
man

explanation.surface: A suave fellow by day turns out to be a fairy after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Smooth looks like an adjective describing the chap; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore the Sandman sprinkles sand in children's eyes to bring sleep at bedtime.

clue.text: Dog that's left on the bridge

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so these pieces follow the bridge

parts.note: a span is a bridge, or the stretch of one between supports
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A ship's dog has been abandoned on the captain's bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge suggests a ship, where left would be port; here it is simply a span, and left is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of gun dog with long drooping ears and a silky coat.

clue.text: After winter what turnarounds in food from the Orient!

parts.note: spring is the season that follows winter
rolls are turns over and over

explanation.surface: A seasonal menu of reversed dishes from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring rolls are fried pancake rolls stuffed with vegetables, a staple of Chinese cuisine.

clue.text: Vegetable requiring an even cut

parts.note: par in golf is the standard score, so being at par means level or even
a snip is a small cut made with scissors

explanation.surface: A cook is told the vegetable must be chopped into equal pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even cut' reads as a cooking instruction, but even and cut are two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale, sweet root grown and eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Political reforms abroad operate with risk

definitions.note: the answer names one programme of reform, used as a collective

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reforms in a foreign country are carried out at some peril.
explanation.walkthrough: Abroad also hints that the answer is a foreign (Russian) word.
explanation.definitionFit: Perestroika was Gorbachev's programme of restructuring the Soviet economy and government in the 1980s.

clue.text: Think about game 20 played

parts.note: rugby union is abbreviated RU

indicators.note: the letters of that answer are played about with, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to clue 20, which is inmate

explanation.surface: Someone considers how a match involving clue 20 went.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 20 points to the answer of 20 down, whose letters are rearranged here.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to ponder or turn something over slowly in the mind.

clue.text: The Queen is by the bedroom window

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a shared bedroom
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: Her Majesty stands beside the window of her bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bedroom window' looks like one phrase defining the answer, but bedroom gives a piece and only window defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormer is a window set upright in a sloping roof, often lighting an attic bedroom.

clue.text: Charlie is in New York, chasing fashionable answer to bankruptcy

indicators.note: the New York piece follows behind the others

parts.note: in, as in style
to solve is to find the answer

indicators.note: Charlie sits inside New York's letters

parts.note: C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A trendy New York firm finds a solution to going bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvency is the state of being unable to pay debts, the condition behind bankruptcy.

clue.text: A right to be in the city? Never!

indicators.note: the first two pieces are to be placed within the city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York, the city
taken as written

explanation.surface: An outraged citizen refuses to accept that anyone has a right to live in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Nary is a dialect word meaning not one or not ever, as in nary a word.

clue.text: Tennis star playing people passing through

indicators.note: the tennis player is playing about, so the letters of tennis star are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tennis champion at a tournament draws crowds of visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Transients are people who stay only briefly in a place before moving on.

clue.text: Verse the clergyman mostly cut?

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a cleric is a member of the clergy
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: A poem asks whether the vicar has trimmed most of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a comic four-line biographical poem, named after Edmund Clerihew Bentley.

clue.text: How 18 lost a turn?

definitions.meaning: the tsar of Russia, the answer to 18, lost his throne through the 1917 uprising
a single rotation, one complete turn of a wheel

explanation.walkthrough: The 18 refers to the answer TSAR; the Russian Revolution ended the reign of Nicholas II.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a political overthrow and a single full rotation about an axis.

clue.text: Called, having struggled across to look after baby

indicators.note: the struggled word stretches across the babysitting word, enclosing it

parts.note: vied, competed
to sit, as in babysit

explanation.surface: A babysitter phoned after a fight over who would mind the child.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone is to visit them, so called here means paid a visit.

clue.text: Apartments arranged to accommodate a ruler

indicators.note: the two words accommodate the answer, which sits inside them across the word break

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second hold the letters

explanation.surface: Flats are set out to house a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Arranged looks like an anagram signal, but the ruler is simply lodged inside the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia before 1917, an absolute monarch.

clue.text: Protective covering for marine mammal worker

parts.note: a seal
the worker ant is crossword shorthand for a worker

explanation.surface: Someone who works with seals needs waterproof gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant is a coating applied to make a surface watertight or airtight.

clue.text: One serving time is an item, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may be put another way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A prisoner is described as just another item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is an item' sounds like a romantic pairing; it is material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a prisoner, someone doing time in jail.

clue.text: Desire comes before soldiers shine

indicators.note: the desire piece is placed ahead of the soldiers piece

parts.note: lust is strong desire
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A soldier's longing for polish precedes the parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the gleam or sheen on a polished surface.

clue.text: Devious controller leaving work on Sunday

indicators.note: used as a verb, to work the letters of leaving is to knead them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sly boss quits his job on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving work' reads as quitting a job; in fact leaving is the material and work the signal to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the hypnotist in du Maurier's Trilby, gave his name to anyone who manipulates another person for sinister ends.

clue.text: Make-up supplied by friends turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pals

explanation.surface: Friends arrive carrying cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap is informal British slang for cosmetics, especially heavily applied face paint.

clue.text: Posed in front of church and fell, dropping case and bag

indicators.note: the posing piece goes ahead of church

parts.note: sat, as for a portrait

indicators.note: the outside letters of fell are its case, and they are dropped to leave the centre

parts.note: the word fell with its first and last letters stripped off

explanation.surface: Someone poses outside a church, trips, and loses both suitcase and handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: Fell looks like a verb of falling; here it is just a word whose outer letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, traditionally carried by schoolchildren for books.

clue.text: Falls once more returning with artist

indicators.note: the word for once more is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: again
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: An artist keeps going back to paint a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Falls looks like a verb; it is the famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the name of the great waterfalls on the border between New York State and Ontario.

clue.text: Went out empty and won the deposit

indicators.note: letters that went out of their places are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler left the room broke yet still won back the stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A down payment is the initial sum paid on a purchase, with the balance due later, much like a deposit.
